description: Add a scrollable Rules screen (? key) and an About box (A key) as modal overlays to the existing Yahtzee TUI. Neither feature touches existing game logic, keybindings, or the scoreboard.

userStories.title: Create pyproject.toml with package metadata
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a pyproject.toml so that the app has a canonical version number accessible both via importlib.metadata (when installed) and via direct file parsing (when run from source).
acceptanceCriteria: pyproject.toml exists at the project root
[project] table contains name = "yahtzee" and version = "0.1.0"
[build-system] table is present (use hatchling or setuptools — whichever requires no extra install beyond the existing venv)
Running `python -c "import importlib.metadata; print(importlib.metadata.version('yahtzee'))"` after `pip install -e .` prints 0.1.0
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Write rules content file
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a Markdown file with the complete Yahtzee rules so the Rules screen has content to display.
acceptanceCriteria: File exists at yahtzee/assets/rules.md (create yahtzee/assets/ directory)
Contains an Objective section explaining the goal of the game (maximize score over 13 turns)
Contains a Turn Flow section: roll up to 3 times, hold dice between rolls, score exactly one category per turn
Contains an Upper Section section covering Ones through Sixes (sum of matching face value) and the Upper Bonus rule (score >= 63 → +35 bonus)

Contains a Lower Section section with all 7 categories: Three of a Kind (sum all dice if 3+ match), Four of a Kind (sum all dice if 4+ match), Full House (25 pts), Small Straight (30 pts), Large Straight (40 pts), Yahtzee (50 pts), Chance (sum all dice)
Contains a Scoring a Zero section explaining a player may score any unscored category as 0
File is well-formed Markdown (headings, lists, bold for point values) — no HTML tags
File is loadable by textual.widgets.Markdown without errors
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement RulesScreen modal
userStories.description: As a player, I want to open a scrollable rules overlay with ? so I can read the rules without leaving the game.
acceptanceCriteria: New file yahtzee/rules_screen.py containing class RulesScreen(ModalScreen)
RulesScreen composes a ScrollableContainer (or VerticalScroll if ScrollableContainer is unavailable in Textual 8.0.0) wrapping a Markdown widget
Markdown widget loads yahtzee/assets/rules.md at compose time using Path(__file__).parent / 'assets' / 'rules.md'
Overlay is approximately 80% of terminal width and 90% of terminal height, centered
Content is scrollable with up/down arrow keys
Pressing Escape dismisses the screen and returns focus to the game
Pressing ? while RulesScreen is open also dismisses it (toggle behaviour)
A hint line at the bottom reads: '  ↑/↓ scroll  ·  Esc or ? close  ' in muted color (#8b949e)
Border is solid or round in color #3fb950 (green) — distinct from existing red/orange modals
Background is #16213e (consistent with existing modals)
CSS is inline on the class — no separate .tcss file
No new Python dependencies introduced
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Wire ? keybinding in app.py
userStories.description: As a player, I want pressing ? at any point during the game to open the Rules screen so help is always one keystroke away.
acceptanceCriteria: app.py imports RulesScreen from yahtzee.rules_screen
BINDINGS in YahtzeeApp gains entry ("question_mark", "show_rules", "Rules")
action_show_rules() calls self.push_screen(RulesScreen())
action_show_rules() is a no-op when another modal is already open — guard with `if len(self.screen_stack) == 1` before pushing
Footer displays '? Rules' hint automatically via BINDINGS
No existing keybinding (r, n, q) is displaced
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement AboutScreen modal
userStories.description: As a player, I want to press A to open a centered About box showing version and runtime info so I can quickly check what version of the game I'm running.
acceptanceCriteria: New file yahtzee/about_screen.py containing class AboutScreen(ModalScreen)
Dialog has a double-line border in color #79c0ff (blue) — distinct from all existing modals
Dialog width is 50 columns, height is auto, centered on screen

Dialog displays in order: title 'YAHTZEE' in bold #79c0ff, blank line, Version line, Author line (AUTHOR constant set to the real author name), Python version (sys.version_info major.minor.micro), Textual version (importlib.metadata.version('textual')), blank line, one-line description centered, blank line, dismiss hint in muted color #8b949e

Version is resolved with three-step fallback: (1) importlib.metadata.version('yahtzee'), on PackageNotFoundError (2) tomllib.loads(Path('pyproject.toml').read_text())['project']['version'] using `import tomllib` (Python >= 3.11) wrapped in try/except ImportError to attempt `import tomli as tomllib` for Python 3.10, on any exception (3) fall back to '0.1.0-dev'
Pressing Enter, Space, or Escape dismisses the screen
CSS is inline on the class — no separate .tcss file
Typecheck passes
